ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Governed by the Companies Act 1993, the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), the Financial Markets Authority Act 2011, the Companies (Disclosure of Ultimate Ownership) Amendment Act 2023, the Sanctions Act 2022, and the Privacy Act 2020. The New Zealand UBO disclosure obligation is implemented through the Companies Office: companies must obtain and hold ultimate ownership information and provide it to the Registrar of Companies. That UBO record is not a public register; it is restricted to government and law-enforcement access. For any Chinese parent or shareholder, the PRC PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 (effective 1 November 2024) separately requires Chinese-side UBO disclosure to Chinese government authorities, but that Chinese law is not the operative UBO regime for the New Zealand entity itself.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: the registry-issued Certificate of Incorporation is used directly; obtain an Apostille from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) for use in any Apostille Convention country. Consular Legalization route for a non-member destination: obtain MFAT attestation of the registrar's signature and then submit the document to the consulate or embassy of the destination jurisdiction for consular legalization. Never apply both the Apostille and consular legalization to the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: obtain the Certificate of Good Standing from the Companies Office and then attach an Apostille issued by MFAT. Consular Legalization route for non-Hague countries: after MFAT attestation of the registrar's signature, submit to the receiving state's consulate in New Zealand for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for pre-incorporation and corporate banking matters
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of NZ Ltd, notarized by a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: the board resolution must be notarized by a New Zealand notary public, then the notary signature is covered by an Apostille issued by MFAT. Consular Legalization route for non-member jurisdictions: after notarization and MFAT attestation, the document is consular-legalized by the competent consulate of the destination country. Do not add an Apostille to the same document that is being consular-legalized.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders and directors of NZ Ltd, registered with the New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: certified copy of the registered constitution is notarized and then apostilled by MFAT if the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille state. Consular Legalization route: notarized certified copy is authenticated by MFAT and then legalized by the consulate of the destination jurisdiction; the Apostille route and consular route are parallel and never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand registered bank under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989, holding the company's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: the bank reference letter is signed by a bank officer, notarized if required by the receiving institution, and then Apostilled by MFAT. Consular Legalization route for non-Hague destinations: after notarization and MFAT attestation of the bank officer's signature, the document is submitted to the destination jurisdiction's consulate for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are exclusive alternatives and must never appear in sequence on the same instrument.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), particularly sections 12-16 (Incorporation), 20-21 (Name of Company), 31-34 (Constitution), 122-124 (Directors), 128-130 (Shareholders), 189-190 (Registered Office)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a division of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Form 1) filed online via the Companies Office website
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement for a limited liability company. Shares may be issued at par value without any initial payment, subject to solvency requirements and the company's constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company')

Held at [Registered Office Address], on [Date], at [Time].

Present: [Director 1], [Director 2], [Director 3] (if any), constituting a quorum.

1. ADOPTION OF CONSTITUTION: RESOLVED that the Constitution of the Company, as tabled, be and is hereby adopted as the constitution of the Company, and that the directors be authorized to file the same with the Companies Office.

2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the initial share capital of the Company be set at [number] ordinary shares of NZ$[par value] each, and that the subscribers to the memorandum of association, as listed in the incorporation application, be allotted the shares as set out in the share register. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors be and are hereby authorized to issue share certificates to the shareholders upon receipt of payment, if any, and to record the allotment in the Company's share register.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the Company open a bank account with [Bank Name], and that the following persons be and are hereby appointed as authorized signatories: [Name], [Name], and [Name]. RESOLVED FURTHER that any two of the authorized signatories shall sign all cheques, drafts, and other instruments on behalf of the Company, and that the bank be furnished with a certified copy of this resolution.

4. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be situated at [Address], and that the Company's records be filed at that address. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Company's agent for service of process be [Name/Address].

5. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as the Managing Director, [Name] be the Company Secretary, and [Name] be the Chief Financial Officer, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until removed by the Board. RESOLVED FURTHER that the officers are authorized to execute all documents and undertake all actions necessary to carry out the Company's business.

6. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the directors and officers be and are hereby authorized to take all steps necessary to register the Company for tax, GST, and any other statutory requirements, and to obtain any necessary permits or licenses.

All resolutions were passed unanimously.

Certified by: [Chairman's Signature]

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Companies Office register to ensure the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name. Reserve the name if required. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. Submit a name reservation application online, providing the proposed name and a brief description of the intended business activities. The application must be accompanied by a declaration that the name is not offensive or misleading. The reservation is valid for 20 working days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may appeal to the Companies Office within 10 working days, or choose an alternative name and submit a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the incorporation application (Form 1) providing details of the company name, registered office address, directors, shareholders, and share structure. Each director must consent to act and provide their full name, residential address, and date of birth. The application must be signed by all shareholders or their authorized agents. Pay the filing fee via credit card or direct debit. Upon approval, the Companies Office will issue a Certificate of Incorporation and a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director for each director
Registered office address (must be a physical address in New Zealand)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, the Companies Office will provide reasons. Correct the deficiencies and resubmit. If the rejection is based on name, choose a new name and reapply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the company must register for income tax and GST (if annual turnover exceeds NZ$60,000 or voluntarily). Use the IRD online portal (myIR) to register the company, providing the NZBN, company details, and contact information. The company will receive an IRD number and GST number. If employees will be hired, register for PAYE. Registration is mandatory within 30 days of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, contact IRD to expedite. Ensure all information is accurate to avoid penalties. If the application is queried, provide additional documentation as requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks in New Zealand (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a bank and schedule an account opening appointment. Provide the company's incorporation certificate, NZBN, constitution (if any), and a board resolution authorizing the account opening and specifying signatories. The bank will conduct due diligence checks, including beneficial ownership verification. Provide identification for all directors and signatories. The account will be activated after verification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional documentation, provide it promptly. If the application is declined, consider another bank or provide additional evidence of business ownership and legitimacy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; online portal: myIR Secure Online Services (https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir). New Zealand Customs Service operates the border and export clearance platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For NZ_LTD, a New Zealand resident limited company: (1) incorporate under the Companies Act 1993 with the New Zealand Companies Office and obtain the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN); (2) apply for the IRD number through the IRD using the myIR company registration channel, or receive it automatically from Companies Office data sharing; the IRD number is the single national TIN and is also the GST registration number; (3) register for GST at the same time if taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period, or voluntarily before starting operations; (4) if the company is established by foreign shareholders, provide the ultimate shareholder and beneficial owner details for AML/CFT customer due diligence. For a foreign non-resident entity not resident in New Zealand but deriving New Zealand-source income or supplying remote services to New Zealand consumers, the entity must separately apply for a non-resident IRD number via Inland Revenue's non-resident registration procedures in myIR, supplying its foreign registration certificate, constitution, director and tax-residency details, and an agent for service in New Zealand if required. The IRD number must be quoted on all GST returns, income tax returns, tax invoices, and export documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no US-style check-the-box election. The default tax classification for a New Zealand limited company is separate entity-level taxation at the 28% corporate income tax rate on worldwide income. An eligible close-held company may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) treatment under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, causing income and deductions to flow through to shareholders; this election must be made to IRD within the statutory timeframe and imposes strict eligibility requirements. There is no elective hybrid-mismatch treatment; New Zealand hybrid mismatch rules apply mandatorily. Under GST, related resident companies may elect group registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, treating the group as a single registered person.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies supplied in any 12-month period in the course of a New Zealand taxable activity; registration becomes compulsory when the threshold is met or expected to be met. Non-resident suppliers of remote services are also required to register when their supplies to New Zealand resident consumers exceed NZD 60,000 in 12 months. Entities may voluntarily register below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not impose a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or anti-fraud digital stamping mandate. Electronic invoicing through the Peppol network is voluntary; businesses may also issue PDF or paper tax invoices. GST returns must be filed electronically via myIR at the registered filing frequency. Tax invoices must contain prescribed particulars under the GST Act, and there is no IRD API pre-approval or stamping requirement for invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand within 28 days after the time of supply and retains evidence of export. Services are zero-rated under section 11(2) when supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, excluding services supplied directly in connection with land in New Zealand or with tangible personal property located in New Zealand and not exported. For the hyper-casual gaming business, advertising inventory supplied to non-resident ad networks such as the AdMob and AppLovin payout entities, and digital content services supplied to overseas platform customers, may qualify for zero-rating as services to non-residents; free-to-play user access itself is not a taxable supply. The supplier must hold contracts, ad-network settlement and payout statements, user and platform location evidence, and records demonstrating the non-resident status and offshore consumption of the service. For pure digital services, a New Zealand Customs export declaration and physical transport documents are inapplicable; the digital substantiation package is the contract, platform payout statements, and foreign exchange credit evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Export Entry (lodged under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 through the Trade Single Window system)
Bill of Lading, sea waybill, or air waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and GST tax invoice showing the supplier IRD number, zero-rated treatment, and export or non-resident recipient details

Bank foreign-exchange credit advice, SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 payment message, or platform payout statement evidencing receipt of proceeds from the offshore customer or ad network; New Zealand does not issue a statutory Inward Remittance Certificate, so the bank or payment-rail evidence is the

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates under a fully floating exchange-rate regime, and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not administer exchange controls, bilateral payments agreements, or capital-repatriation licensing. The current account is fully open: dividends, interest, royalties, profits, and loan repayments may be freely converted to any foreign currency and remitted offshore without central-bank approval or any surrender condition. The capital account is equally open for standard equity and debt injections, and non-residents may hold 100% of a local limited company; the only constraints arise under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for acquisitions of sensitive land or significant business assets above statutory thresholds, neither of which applies to a hyper-casual mobile-game publishing entity owning intellectual property. There is no statutory obligation to convert export proceeds generated by AdMob or AppLovin payouts into NZD, no holding period for foreign receipts, and no income tax or withholding surcharge on distribution beyond normal imputation and Non-resident Withholding Tax on outbound dividends. The practical profit-remittance hurdle is therefore limited to tax-clearance documentation: directors must file accurate GST and income-tax returns and issue a shareholder and tax reconciliation to support the economic substance of the gaming operation before a bank permits a large one-off dividend wire. Overall, New Zealand scores as a zero-exchange-control, fully convertible jurisdiction for a standard software and intellectual-property treasury.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand does not impose export-proceeds surrender or conversion requirements. A resident or non-resident-owned NZ Ltd may retain 100% of all foreign-currency earnings in any permitted currency, onshore or offshore, and may repatriate the balance of an AdMob or AppLovin settlement account to its NZD clearing account at a time of its choosing. The only statutory timeline is the balance-of-payments and financial-reporting deadline: a company must ensure that the Reserve Bank statistical collection via its bank automatically reports any inbound settlement wire within the same business day; no manual conversion window exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (Business Everyday NZD with USD ledger)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Limited but usable as a settlement funnel only. A fintech EMI that is not a Registered Bank under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 cannot lawfully accept deposits or provide NZD clearing-house access; such firms operate under a money-remittance and service-provider regime with disclosure duties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Practically, an overseas EMI may hold variable-balance USD wallets for ad-network payouts and issue virtual cards, but it cannot issue New Zealand bank account numbers, cannot be named as the company's statutory banker for GST/IRD reconciliation, and cannot process inward correspondent flows on the NZ Clearing System. For a compliant treasury, the EMI should be used only to collect AdMob/AppLovin USD settlements before sweeping to a primary domestic ADI; the primary legal banking relationship must sit with ANZ, BNZ, ASB, or Westpac.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed NZ Ltd with non-resident shareholders, the majority of Tier-1 domestic banks mandate an in-person introduction meeting at their commercial banking centre for at least one of the statutory directors or an appointed local authorised signatory. Remote video KYC is occasionally permitted if the director's passport and proof-of-address are covered by an apostille or consular legalisation, but in practice a bank compliance committee usually requires a physical appearance for entities deriving revenue from overseas ad networks. A consular proxy opening, where a non-resident director authenticates before a New Zealand embassy without an in-branch visit, is offered only by one or two mid-tier banks and almost never granted for an entity without prior banking history. The cleaner onboarding path is to authorise a local registered director or accountant as signatory and have that person appear in branch with the original company documents, while the non-resident principal completes the customer due diligence questionnaire via video before the physical visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership in a single-shareholder NZ shelf company with no local operational footprint; the bank treats this as a potential shell treasury-structure for money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full certification of the beneficial-ownership register (10% or more holders) in the bank's template, certified passports, five years of address history, recent utility bills for each beneficial owner, a current Companies Office extract showing the registered office, a group-structure diagram explaining the parent company's commercial rationale, and a notarised source-of-wealth letter from the shareholder's private-banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity settlement credits from AdMob and AppLovin arriving daily in micro-transactions with no clearly identifiable underlying contractual counterparty; possible layering of ad-fraud proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly payout reports generated by the ad networks for the preceding six months, matched by display name to the publisher app ID; executed Google AdMob Terms and AppLovin Publisher Agreement; SDK integration screenshots showing active users, install counts, and platform billing receipts; and a signed director's declaration that no deceptive ad traffic or financial fraud is present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity capital in USD from a jurisdiction on the FATF grey-list, immediately followed by an equivalent onward payment to a software developer; possible obfuscated conversion of illegal dark-web receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference and six-month statement of the remitting shareholder's account at the source bank; formal board minute and share-allotment resolution detailing the equity subscription amount; signed shareholder loan documents with market-rate interest, repayment schedule, and tax opinion if the incoming funds are a debt instrument; confirmation of tax residence via tax identification number; and either a notarised sale-and-purchase contract if the funds derive from a business sale or a payslip and savings narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The NZ entity's only local expenses are the registered agent and an outsourced accountant while 100% of operating costs are paid to foreign software contractors, triggering round-tripping and phantom-substance alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party agreements, technical specifications, and milestone invoices from the contractors; source-code repository access logs or project-management history confirming development activity; a current local lease or co-working agreement for the registered office; a local resident director's CV and arm's-length engagement letter; and GST and income-tax filings with the New Zealand Inland Revenue Department corroborating that the entity's substance is intellectual-property ownership and publishing, not a phantom payroll.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share-capital or shareholder-loan injections from non-resident shareholders should be remitted by SWIFT MT103 from an account in the shareholder's name to the NZ Ltd's domestic ADI account. The bank must be instructed to allocate the funds to the company's registered share-allotment ledger rather than to ordinary trade receivables; the MT103 field 70 should include a purpose text such as 'EQUITY INJECTION PER BOARD RESOLUTION DATED ...' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN AGREEMENT NO. ...'. Under the AMLCFT Act, the bank will match the debit side to the shareholder's bank statement and complete a source-of-funds check. For New Zealand purposes, no exchange-control approval or overseas-investment clearance is required unless the investment is considered a significant business asset, which is usually far above the target company's valuation. Capital verification is satisfied by an updated Companies Office register and an auditor's capital-confirmation certificate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade and licensing settlements should use the NZCH bank-to-bank clearing rails for NZD-denominated payments and SWIFT MT103 for foreign-currency wires. For high-value game-software procurement or exclusive IP acquisitions, the treasury should open an advice-based commercial letter of credit (MT700) with the domestic ADI in favour of the offshore contractor, and for documentary collections use MT400 with shipping or performance certificates only when the counterparty is a known long-term vendor. All outbound disbursements must be reconciled to the underlying contract and invoice, and an AML sanction-screening hit will require the company to produce a customs or end-use certificate, particularly where contractor payments are destined for jurisdictions not covered by a designated tax treaty.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD/USD forward contracts, via onshore ADI, with tenor maturity up to 12 months and bilateral credit lines; settlement at maturity delivers the contracted exchange amount.
FX options, both European calls and puts, booked onshore by Tier-1 banks to protect future ad-network USD conversions against adverse NZD movements, with the premium expensed.
Cross-currency basis swaps, USD floating to NZD floating, only to hedge long-term shareholder loan instruments; each swap must be evidenced by an underlying debt obligation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's recorded return date, which is normally the anniversary of incorporation or the date agreed by shareholders as the annual return date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$50 (approx. US$30) per month or part-month per entity, and NZ$50 per month per director, each capped at NZ$1,000 (approx. US$600). If the annual return remains unfiled after the due date, the Registrar issues a 28-day removal notice under the Companies Act 1993; persistent non-filing leads to administrative strike-off and forfeiture of the company name.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue, Government of New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The 7th day of the seventh month after the balance date; for a standard 31 March balance date, the annual IR4 is due by 7 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 (approx. US$150), increased by NZ$250 per month or part-month while the return remains outstanding, up to a maximum of NZ$1,000 (approx. US$600). Underpayments attract use-of-money interest (UOMI) at the IRD prescribed rate (currently around 8.9% p.a., adjusted quarterly). Continued non-filing allows IRD to make a default assessment, issue debt collection action, and petition for liquidation; there is no automatic company strike-off, but unpaid tax can trigger insolvency proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Financial Statements and Auditor's Report Filing (if non-exempt or large)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the directors approve the financial statements, and in any case before the next annual shareholders' meeting; for 'large' and FMC reporting entities, the filing must also be completed within the annual filing cycle set by the Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 / Companies Act 1993, with fines up to NZ$10,000 (approx. US$6,000) per director; continuing failure after Registrar notice may lead to deregistration. Misleading financial statements attract additional civil penalties under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue, Government of New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard two-monthly periods; e.g., the taxable period ending 30 April is due by 28 June, and the period ending 30 June is due by 28 August. If the company has been approved for an annual GST cycle, the return is due by the 28th day of the month following the end of the annual GST period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 (approx. US$150) per month or part-month, capped at NZ$1,000 (approx. US$600). Late payment penalties start at 1% immediately, an additional 4% seven days later, and then 1% per month thereafter; use-of-money interest accrues on all overdue amounts. Persistent GST non-compliance may cause IRD to increase filing frequency and refer the debt for enforced recovery or liquidation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (s45) and the Companies Act 1993, an independent statutory audit is mandatory where the company: (1) is a 'large company', meaning that in the preceding accounting period it had total assets at balance date exceeding NZ$60,000,000 (approx. US$36,000,000), OR total annual revenue exceeding NZ$30,000,000 (approx. US$18,000,000), OR 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees; (2) is an FMC reporting entity such as an issuer of financial products or manager of a licensed fund; (3) has a shareholder holding 5% or more of the voting shares who validly requests an auditor's appointment; or (4) is directed by the Registrar or the company's constitution to undergo an audit. A zero-revenue or small hyper-casual game studio in New Zealand will generally remain exempt unless one of these triggers is crossed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand accounting and financial reporting standards are issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB). Tier 1 for-profit entities must apply NZ IFRS (New Zealand equivalents of International Financial Reporting Standards). Tier 2 for-profit entities may apply NZ IFRS with reduced disclosure concessions (NZ IFRS RDR). Small and medium private companies may prepare financial statements using the XRB's simplified Tasmania or Tier 2/'Small' guidelines; non-exempt large companies must present full NZ IFRS compliant general-purpose financial statements. Audits must be conducted by an independent licensed auditor under the Auditor Regulation Act 2011.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no standalone annual UBO confirmation filing for private limited companies as of the current regulatory cycle. Under the Companies Act 1993, the company must maintain a current register of members and register of directors. Any allotment of shares must be notified to the New Zealand Companies Office within 20 working days; any change in director particulars (name, address, date of birth) must also be lodged within 20 working days. Transfers of existing shares must be recorded in the company's own register of members immediately and share certificates issued within 10 working days; no public filing is required unless the transfer triggers a change of director/registered-office particulars. The AML/CFT Act 2009 requires the entity to identify and verify beneficial owners for non-face-to-face online payment arrangements (such as AdMob and AppLovin payouts); the beneficial ownership information must be maintained internally and refreshed at least annually or whenever any material ownership change occurs.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Allotments and Transfers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$250 – US$800 per annum for a professional New Zealand registered agent and registered-office service, including company secretarial maintenance and registry correspondence handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$6,500 – US$25,000 per annum for a certified independent audit of a simple New Zealand private limited liability company, depending on transaction volume, intercompany balances, and the complexity of the gateway/ad-monetization revenue contracts

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Research and development tax credit of 15% of eligible expenditure (net of subsidies) available for qualifying software development activities. Full immediate deduction for certain low-value assets (under NZD 5,000). Significant tax incentives for software-as-a-service and digital content development through the R&D Tax Incentive regime, subject to approval by New Zealand Trade and Enterprise (NZTE).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 - Company Income Tax Return; accessed via the Inland Revenue 'myIR' electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be filed and the terminal tax (if any) paid by the 7th day of the fourth month after balance date for a standard 31 March balance date (i.e., 7 July). For a non-standard balance date, the deadline adjusts accordingly, and non-resident companies may apply for a provisional due date extension to the 7th day of the eleventh month after balance date, subject to IR discretion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose total gross income: all revenue from hyper-casual mobile game publishing, including ad monetization proceeds from AdMob and AppLovin
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a New Zealand permanent establishment (PE) must include all New Zealand-sourced income attributable to the PE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses and deductions: development costs, user acquisition costs, platform fees, licensing royalties, hosting, and administrative overhead
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be apportioned to the New Zealand PE on an arm's length basis in accordance with the OECD authorised OECD approach (AOA)
Ensure any transfer pricing adjustments under Part F of the Income Tax Act 2007 are reflected

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward and offset (subject to the 5-year time bar and business continuity test under section IA5 of the Income Tax Act 2007)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must satisfy the same ownership and business continuity tests to claim loss carryforward; losses of a foreign PE are quarantined unless separately allowed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, including R&D tax credit, foreign dividend credits, and imputation credits (if any)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may claim credits under double tax agreements (DTAs) for foreign withholding taxes, but are not eligible for the Australian imputation credit component
Payment via myIR; non-resident companies with no New Zealand bank account must arrange for wire transfer to the IRD foreign currency account

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 for each month or part-month that the IR4 remains unfiled, capped at NZD 1,000. In addition, a late payment penalty of 1% immediately, a further 4% after 7 days, and an incremental 1% per month thereafter. Use-of-money interest (UOMI) is charged on any unpaid amount at a prescribed rate, which is adjusted quarterly by the IRD. Failure to file can also trigger judicial fines up to NZD 25,000 per conviction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 28% (non-resident withholding tax, NRWT, on gross dividends). The rate applies to any deemed dividend or actual dividend paid by a New Zealand resident company to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced rate under a relevant double tax agreement (e.g., a 15% treaty rate on dividends through a 10% or 20% voting interest test), the non-resident shareholder must provide a valid certificate of residence (Form IR290 for treaty relief) to the New Zealand company before the dividend is paid. The form must be completed by the foreign tax authority and submitted to the New Zealand payer; the payer then applies the reduced NRWT rate at source. A refund of any over-withheld amount can be claimed using IRDS (Income Tax - DTA refund) form through myIR. Retroactive treaty relief is not available unless the certificate was in place when the dividend was paid.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory NRWT rate is 15% (subject to reduction under applicable DTA, commonly 0% or 10% if the beneficial owner bears the economic cost of intellectual property licensing). Interest: statutory NRWT rate is 15%; DTA relief may reduce to 0% or 10% subject to the anti-treaty-shopping rules. Both are subject to the supplementary dividend regime under sections RE 18 and RP 4.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File thresholds: Complete documentation is required for transactions with associated non-resident enterprises if the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds NZD 1,000,000 for acquisitions of goods and services (including advertising revenue sharing, platform payouts, and IP licensing), and NZD 100,000 for financing transactions. Entities above the threshold must prepare a Local File and, where the group's consolidated turnover exceeds NZD 250,000,000, a Master File and annual CbC report (threshold of NZD 250,000,000). Contemporaneous documentation must be in place at the time of the transaction or adoption of the return, and be available for the IRD within 45 days of request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime as in Cayman/BVI. However, the IRD applies the general anti-avoidance rule (section BG 1) and the specific transfer pricing provisions (Part F, subpart GD) to disregard transactions that lack commercial substance. A New Zealand resident company must demonstrate real decision-making and operational substance in New Zealand; otherwise, the IRD may re-characterize or allocate profits to the jurisdiction of economic substance. For a hyper-casual games developer, substance is evidenced by board meetings in New Zealand, local game design and engineering staff, and the maintenance of patent/copyright ownership records. Thin capitalization rules (net debt to assets ratio of 60% for non-resident-owned groups) also impose an implicit substance requirement on debt levels.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of ad monetization revenue (e.g., AdMob and AppLovin payments) on the IR4, understatement of taxable turnover, or destruction of accounting records to avoid tax on foreign income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction for tax evasion under sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994. Imprisonment up to 5 years and unlimited fine at the court's discretion. A further civil penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall if the evasion involved a dominant purpose of avoiding tax (shortfall penalty under section 141E).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns may be jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall under the Companies Act 1993, and also be personally prohibited from managing a company. Criminal conviction can lead to director disqualification for up to 5 years and cancellation of travel rights.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a New Zealand company without physical presence, a New Zealand resident director with substantive knowledge, or actual performance of core income-generating activities in New Zealand; used as a conduit entity for international advertising revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IRD may disregard the corporate structure under section BG 1 and attribute the income to the actual recipient onshore. Additionally, the company may be liable for a shortfall penalty of up to 100% of the resulting tax, and the company name may be deregistered under the Companies Act for carrying on a 'zero substance' operation with a non-material place of business. Inland Revenue may also issue a notice under section 17 of the TAA to access bank records of platform payouts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who permit the company to operate as a shell without genuine economic substance in New Zealand may be personally liable for the tax avoidance consequence under the 'abuse of corporate personality' doctrine. Courts may pierce the corporate veil and order the director to repay the full tax arrears, plus compound interest and penalties. In egregious cases, a director's travel is restricted by the High Court upon IRD application.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving ad monetization payouts from foreign platforms while failing to conduct a risk assessment, non-media customer due diligence, or beneficial ownership verification on business partners outside New Zealand, or failing to report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009: up to NZD 2,000,000 for a body corporate per offence, plus an additional NZD 10,000 per day for continuing violations by a reporting entity, if the entity performs a money or value transfer service. If a gaming publisher acts as a payment intermediary (which is atypical for pure advertising), it must register with the Department of Internal Affairs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be criminally liable for an AML/CFT offence if they are knowingly a party to a breach or fail to ensure the company's compliance. Penalties include imprisonment for up to 2 years and fines up to NZD 50,000 for individuals. A director can also be subject to a disqualification order under the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mischaracterizing the licence of the hyper-casual game IP to an offshore affiliate at an artificially lower royalty rate, or entering into a cost-sharing arrangement with the offshore entity that allocates the majority of high-margin profits offshore without a corresponding contribution of value
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may reassess taxable income using the arm's length price and impose a shortfall penalty of up to 40% of the underpaid tax for a merely tax-disloyal arrangement, and up to 20% if the taxpayer has not taken reasonable care. Interest at the long-term UOMI rate applies on the underpayment. The withholding of NRWT on deemed royalty payments may also be reassessed at 15% (or 0% if DTA relief is substantiated).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who actively set up the offending transfer pricing structure without proper TP documentation may be found personally liable as 'tax loss confirmation agents' under the Tax Administration Act, leading to an order to pay the entire shortfall and penalty. In cases of wilful TP fraud, criminal liability attaches, potentially including 5 years imprisonment and personal travel bans.
